original_question: Is it possible to choose the domain so that the dynamics of the corresponding billiard map are locally (near the 2-periodic orbit) conjugated to the dynamics of the rigid rotation through some angle α?
correct_elements: The draft already captures the core existence question almost verbatim: whether one can choose a billiard domain so that the billiard map, near a distinguished 2-periodic orbit, is locally conjugate to a rigid rotation by angle α.
missing_details: The setting should be identified as the usual planar inner billiard in a smooth strictly convex domain Ω bounded by a smooth curve γ, as established in §4.2(b).
The domain is not arbitrary: the paper requires a convex billiard table “having the symmetry of an ellipse.”
The relevant 2-periodic orbit should be identified as the one along the y-axis.
The existence quantifiers should be explicit: one asks whether there exist both such a domain and some angle α∈R.
The conjugacy is local in phase space for the billiard map, in a neighborhood of that specific 2-periodic orbit, not a global conjugacy of the full billiard dynamics.
The paper does not make any Diophantine condition part of the formal problem statement; α/π being Diophantine is mentioned only as numerical evidence afterward.
refined_question: Does there exist a smooth strictly convex planar billiard table Ω whose boundary has the symmetry of an ellipse, so that the billiard has the 2-periodic orbit along the y-axis, and an angle α∈R such that the corresponding inner billiard map is locally conjugate, in a neighborhood of that 2-periodic orbit in phase space, to the rigid rotation by angle α?
justification: This draft matches the paper’s Problem 4.6 essentially verbatim. The only needed sharpening is to restore the surrounding hypotheses supplied by the nearby context: the standard planar billiard setup from §4.2(b), the ellipse-symmetry assumption stated immediately before the problem, and the identification of the distinguished 2-periodic orbit as the one along the y-axis. I did not strengthen the question to prescribe α or assume a Diophantine condition, because the paper states only an existence problem and presents the Diophantine case merely as supporting numerical evidence.
